chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man: Is it permissible for him to look at his wife when she dies, or to wash her if there is no one else to wash her; and about the woman: Can she look at her husband in a similar manner when he dies? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with that. The family of the woman does so because they dislike for her husband to look at something of her that they dislike.

key_terms.يُغَسِّلَهَا: to wash her (ritual washing of the dead)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to wash his wife's body after death according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of a spouse viewing or washing the other's body is rooted in the practical necessity of the family of the deceased, who often prefer to inspect the body themselves to ensure the spouse does not notice any disliked physical traits. This ruling highlights the nuanced interplay between ritual purity laws and social customs within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the act is not merely a right but a consideration of familial dynamics. The hadith underscores the importance of modesty and mutual respect in death rituals, distinguishing between the legal permissibility and the social etiquette of the time.
